variants.title: Pulse speed on a slinky stretched to 1.2 m
variants.sample: The laboratory's own steel slinky (215 g on the balance), stretched to 1.2 m
variants.method: sideways flick, timed over several lengths
variants.unknown: the speed of the pulse at this stretch
variants.note: The mass per metre is not a property of the material: it is the slinky's own mass divided by the span it is stretched to, so a shorter stretch of the same slinky gives a larger mu.

source.title: Laboratory Manual Science, Class IX, NCERT - velocity of a pulse propagated through a stretched string / slinky
source.note: mu = measured mass of this slinky divided by its span

variants.title: Pulse speed on a tightly stretched slinky
variants.sample: The same steel slinky, stretched to 1.8 m and pulled tight
variants.method: sideways flick at a higher tension, timed over several lengths
variants.unknown: how much faster the pulse runs when the tension is doubled
variants.note: Twice the tension gives the square root of two times the speed, about 1.41 times.
